title: A provisional gate of class secrets or push is answered by an agent with no class check, and --confirm without --by makes it the operator's
goal: A gate of class secrets or push is always blocking and only the operator answers it: `backlog.py gate add` makes a gate whose derived class is secrets or push blocking whatever --kind says; `answer --provisional` and `answer --confirm` refuse such a gate unless `--by operator` is given (a `--confirm` with no `--by` is refused; it no longer defaults to operator); `backlog.py check` reports a provisional gate of such a class; planted-failure tests cover each form (a provisional push gate answered with no --by, --provisional by agent, --confirm with no --by, and gate add --kind provisional); found by the SP-4xngzagf review: a runner takes the recommendation of every provisional gate, so a push or secrets gate added as provisional is answered 'yes' by an agent with no class check

run: set -e; d=$(mktemp -d); git clone -q "$PWD" "$d/r"; cd "$d/r"; f=$(grep -L '"sprint"' kb/_self/backlog/BG-*.json | head -1); id=$(basename "$f" .json); python3 _tools/backlog.py gate add "$id" --kind provisional --id pushgate --question "Push the commits to the public remote?" --option yes --option no --recommendation yes --do "yes=true" --do "no=true" >/dev/null; if python3 _tools/backlog.py answer "$id" pushgate --provisional >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 1; fi

gates.question: Backlog check now errors on provisional gates of the two operator-only classes in other items: convert those gates to blocking in a separate follow-up before this lands?
